## Declared assumptions and kT's decisions

- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** kT declares AOI-2226 refractive-index matching and independently switchable clear/glare/dark plus visible/NIR modulation. NOT demonstrated at full scale. Zero numeric optical/IR cooling performance credited; worst Venus solar aperture heat explicitly included. Transparent dome and AOI thermal expansion/differential heat flux remain OPEN. Decision: Zero quantified thermal attenuation or dynamic optical performance credited. Worst-case glazing heat counted.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-25.** Torch heat package (kT, 2026-10-25): each pellet is wrapped in a shell of remass that soaks up the burn and leaves as exhaust. The shell must let no more than ~358 ppm of the burn's energy escape as light, counting its own glow (the reactor face's 10 MW/m2 limit); the design value is 180 ppm. With the model's other assumptions (torch/torch_heat_inputs.json: light 40% of fusion energy; He3-rich, spin-polarised fuel with 0.76% neutrons, 85% absorbed by the shell; plume contact 1e-4 of charged energy; coil shield transmission 1e-3), 1.40 GW reaches hot structure and 0.48 MW the magnet coils at 12.6 TW of fusion. These are assumptions, not results. Replaces v0.5.1's 387 MW (34 ppm) torch-leak gap. Decision: v0.5.2 torch heat package (kT chose the package and 1,750 K fins on 2026-10-25 and accepted this wording the same day): the remass shell lets no more than ~360 ppm of the burn's energy escape as light, counting its own glow; design value 180 ppm; with the heat model's other assumptions 1.40 GW reaches hot structure and 0.48 MW the magnet coils.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-25.** Hot fins run for life at 1750 K. Lithium heat pipes have run in lab tests to ~1,500 K and briefly ~1,800 K; years at 1750 K with burn cycling and neutron exposure is an engineering extrapolation (a technology milestone), not new physics. Fallback: 1,500 K fins, ~49 m span, ~30 t, still inside the reserve. Decision: kT: "Let's go 1750." Hot fins at 1,750 K, recorded as an engineering extrapolation (technology milestone), with 1,500 K fins as the fallback.
- **ACCEPTED.** Plant electrical: Metric HARD at a 1300 K reject temperature needs 34.8 MW of cryo-chain electrical power, against canon's 23.9 MW at 900 K. The relational plant must supply this (canon amendment), or the cryo chain must reject through a 900 K loop. Decision: canon states the relational plant supplies ~34.8 MW for Metric HARD at a 1,300 K reject temperature. Option not taken: a 900 K loop for the cryo chain.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** At worst-case sunlight, the open crown adds ~100 kW of solar heating to habitat. In heat-pump-failed or cold-running passive backup the 16 Strata gores MUST CLOSE; clear/glare/dark AOI states may not be credited as heat rejection or solar exclusion. Solar absorption/IR-band partition and AOI switching performance are not physically qualified. Decision: Model-derived operating restriction: active open-crown worst Venus sun creates ~100kW load; heat pump failed requires closure. Physical controls remain unqualified.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-31.** Cold running (rev 7, F5 provisional item F5-TE-01): the tunable flanks drop from emissivity 0.85 to 0.1, so at the same skin temperature they radiate 12% as much. Heat is held, not removed: habitat heat 58.1 kW (x1.25), plus plant standby 10.0 kW and cryo standby 10.0 kW, less 7.1 kW still leaking through 177 m2 of low-e skin at 290 K warms the 50 t of protected water by 15 K in about 12.3 h (ideal no-standby ceiling 17.1 h). ENGINEERING_ASSUMPTION (screening placeholders 10+10 kW, NOT sourced or qualified); editable, replace with measured/engineering budget. Then the ship must open the strakes or switch the flanks back to normal. Detailed load-cycle variation, cryo plant duty, tank thermal coupling, and reserve storage remain open. The metallic look in the viewer is a proposed optical property. Decision: Provisional ~17.09h ideal cap before plant and cryo standby; 10+10 kW editable illustrative loads yield a shorter window; physical heat budget OPEN
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** I4 terrace 4 columns sized as 7075-T6 76mm OD x 3mm at 0.49m. 5g x1.5 ultimate +0.5g lateral member screen, no joint, deck bearing, vibration, fatigue, swept-body or 3D egress qualification. HOLLOW: closed only for column members, not system. Decision: kT accepts I4 terrace mounts and structural load paths as DECLARED, not structurally tested to hardware standard. Original 5g×1.5 member / 0.5g lateral assumption remains visible; joints, bearing, vibration and fatigue have not been newly modelled.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-26.** Berth viewports (v0.5.7): 10 x 0.5 m viewports keep the berth screen because acrylic plugs carry at least the g/cm2 they replace (armour 27.14 vs 27.0, ring 8.26 vs 8.0), so the ray screen, which treats the hull as continuous, is unchanged. Rev 3: the same plug kit is in every opening below the crown, including the L2 viewport band, and continues through the storm-shelter jacket (17 cm more acrylic for the 20 cm of water). Not yet shown: the dose. Acrylic is ~8% hydrogen by mass against water's 11%, so per g/cm2 it may stop cosmic-ray secondaries slightly less well; a transport check may ask for a thicker plug. Encapsulated for fire. Decision: Every opening below the crown carries an acrylic shield plug and insert with at least the g/cm2 they replace (armour 27, berth ring 8, shelter jacket 20), so berths and shelter keep their screens with the shutters open; the dose is accepted as a provision until a transport check (OLTARIS) is run; plugs are encapsulated and counted as fire load.
- **AWAITING by kT 2026-10-26.** Rev7 16 closing Strata gores and opening doctrine are retained; their original acceptance applied only to the earlier segmented 2.3m pressure panes, not the new 7m seamless dome. Decision: kT selected TWO independently pressure-capable ~7m ceramic domes with AOI; independent failure mechanism / proof remains open.
- **AWAITING.** kT Option A 2026-11-01: TWO independent full-pressure ~7m transparent ceramic domes, each 28mm/10.5g/cm2, shaped X(r)=2.35-2.15sqrt(1-(r/4.3)^2), backup shifted 0.12m forward. Both must survive loss of the other; 37 outer segmented nonpressure panes +16 closure gores unchanged. 7m monolithic materials fabrication/pressure/impact and optical radiation behaviour UNSHOWN.
- **AWAITING by kT 2026-11-01.** AOI-2226 ~3.023m3 (~3t) gel between two separately sealed pressure domes, gap min normal 5.973cm with backup axial offset ~12cm. Neither pressure-bearing nor a pressure seal. Each independent dome MUST withstand full 101.3kPa after other's failure while optogel is present, WITHOUT shock, fracture, crack bridging or fast pressure-pulse coupling. The research has NO measured high-rate response or independent-shell survival test; do not credit impact damping. Rim slip/contact interfaces and >=56L illustrative thermal-expansion compliance still require engineering. Decision: Both pressure domes must withstand full differential and each others failure with gel in gap, without crack coupling, shock, destructive pressure pulse; physical validation still necessary.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-31.** Habitat armour face (rev 7, kT 2026-10-26): Strata laminate (Builder-derived, MHL-22) over the whole habitat armour, x 0-14. KT_ACCEPTED 2026-10-31 as visible armour face; materials constitutive/physical performance remain OPEN; no changed shielding/mass claim. Bow x 0.0-2.6 m: bare Strata: the erosion face meets the dust flow. Decision: Strata as armour face; constitutive performance OPEN; drone-deployed over-crown armour is OPTION ONLY and drone bay HOLD
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-31.** Metric node faces (rev 7, kT 2026-10-26; Sol: AGREE, placement HOLD): 208 visible flush or recessed faces, 13 rings x 16 at 22.5 deg (rev 5 longeron-study layout). 76 are clear; the rest are flagged: 16 faces dust flow bow first, 12 on bay door, 80 on torch chain, 1 overlaps camera, 2 overlaps hold door, 1 overlaps window, 20 under stowed strake. The design case assumes every face carries at least the armour's g/cm2 it replaces, like the berth-viewport plugs. Sensitivity, faces as open bores through the armour: berth screen 14.71 g/cm2 (31 of 36 berth points below 40) and storm shelter 36.1 g/cm2. So a face must be armour-equivalent: materials, cover, seal and mount stay OPEN, and no dust check exists in the basis yet (faces flagged 'faces dust flow' meet the flow when coasting bow-first). Node stations are not moved for the look; PR #184 stays OPEN. Decision: armour-equivalent g/cm2 per node face; placement HOLD pending PR #184
- **ACCEPTED.** Storm shelter life support: 72 h for 10 people from the life-support room on the same deck (design provision, not computed). Decision: 72 h of life support for 10 people in the storm shelter, from the life-support room on the same deck, recorded as a design provision to be sized in detail later.
- **ACCEPTED.** Galactic cosmic rays: at 2026 free-space rates (1.8 mSv/day, ~657 mSv/yr) a crew member reaches NASA's 600 mSv career limit after ~333 days in deep space. Hull shielding barely changes this. Long careers aboard rely on canon's off-Earth MED-MOD-RADIATION milestone and crew time-in-space rules; this is a canon question, not something the hull can close. Decision: crew protection from galactic cosmic rays relies on canon's off-Earth MED-MOD-RADIATION milestone plus crew time-in-space limits.
- **ACCEPTED.** Torch neutrons and gammas: the shadow shield must attenuate the torch's neutron and gamma output so the dose rate inside the habitat during burns stays within crew limits. The v0.5.2 heat model puts neutrons at ~0.76% of the burn's energy with 85% absorbed by the remass shell; the dose itself is not computed here, only the shadow geometry is checked. Decision: covered by the same declared gap: the torch and shadow shield keep neutron and gamma dose in the habitat within crew limits during burns; the shadow geometry is checked (G6).
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** I4 source-frame check rerun against current geometry. Scene seat length 1.58m <2.10m source crew envelope; 2D seat/ladder/walkways and bare dome clearances NOT physical 3D access or 4g qualification. Crown sightlines are optimistic upper bounds only. All three annulus-floor couches now clear the rectangular terrace in a conservative 3D axis-aligned box test; S4 is moved +0.20m outboard with 0.0541m clearance. This is not occupant-swept collision testing. Optional terrace chamfer NOT BUILT. Decision: kT accepts I4 3D suited-body fit and egress as DECLARED for conventional Wayfarer lab qualification. Bounded plan and 3D couch-versus-terrace AABB tests pass; full physical occupant-swept/4g restraint and evacuation evidence is not represented as newly computed.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-31.** External equipment (rev 7, ENGINEERING_ASSUMPTION): 55 parts from the inventory's 13 item types. Items with a ledger line are located inside it (sensor turrets in mission systems, RF arrays, laser terminals and aft trackers in the avionics racks, forward trackers in the bow sensor ring, service ports in the service arm, vents in life support, the docking target in the collar): 1.86 t, no new mass. New hardware (crawler docks and points, grapple fixtures, EVA rails): 1.42 t from the reserve. Not built: drone_bay HOLD; nav_lights OPTIONAL; crawler_rails NOT YET. Masses are 2026-analogue allowances to be sized. Decision: editable 1.4208t new allowance within dry reserve (2026 analogue guess), 0t sensitivity case required; item positions not frozen
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-10-26.** Torch thrust-vector control: the magnetic nozzle steers the thrust line by up to 1.0 deg (asymmetric coil current). Needed: trim plus an assumed 0.5 deg thrust error (0.848 deg). The error is an engineering assumption, not a measured disturbance history; the authority is not a qualified nozzle capability. Decision: Declare 1 deg of torch thrust-vector authority (decision 2), on the assumed 0.5 deg thrust error.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** Axial RCS: one 25 kN thruster per cluster, canted 10 deg outward (bow ones exhaust forward, aft ones aft). Assumes the plumes clear the crown glazing, hull, hot fins and torch chain; plume impingement is not yet modelled. Decision: kT accepts axial RCS plume clearance as DECLARED, not a new physical plume impingement calculation. Original 10° canted one-nozzle-per-cluster assumption remains.
- **ACCEPTED by kT 2026-11-01.** Long torch burns split into segments of at most 165 min ([V2 6113]) with 15 min coasts (engineering assumption; in free space the coasts change elapsed time, not delta-v). Decision: kT accepts segmented burn doctrine as DECLARED: ≤165min torch burn segments with ≥15min coasts. Coasts add elapsed time, not free-space delta-v. This is not Metric travel qualification.
- **AWAITING by kT 2026-11-01.** Required before treating rendered representation as accepted design evidence; generated images meet source/hash coverage only Decision: New twin-dome + gel viewer/stills require current-hash visual review; prior single-dome review does not transfer.

Script verdict on certification: NOT YET: at least one gate is OPEN or FAIL, or a declared assumption awaits kT. Sign-off still needs both reviewers and loom-gate.

- Method: closed-form plate theory (Navier series for simply supported panels, which is conservative against clamped edges) plus closed-cell equilibrium with tie-webs. A finite-element shell model is the next level of fidelity; the basis does not require it.
